value.a: THE COLLIDING RULING IS AKIEN'S OWN, AND IT RESOLVES IN HIS FAVOUR TWICE OVER. cairn/tools/base/address.py:20-33 records his 2026-08-12 ownership test: 'THE TOP LEVEL OF ~/.cairn/ IS FOR WHAT IS NOT ANY DEVICE'S STATE... the test is not depth, it is OWNERSHIP: a file that answers "what is true of this machine" lives at the top; a file that answers "what is true of this device" lives under devices/<name>/<instance>/.' A device's diagnostic trail answers what is true of that DEVICE, which is why BreadcrumbLog writes to ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/diagnostics.jsonl - the built address is a faithful translation of the 08-12 ruling, not drift. His 2026-08-18 statement puts it under a top-level logs/ root instead. NOT EXCLUSIVE-AND-TERMINAL, and the reconciliation is inside the 08-12 ruling's own words: it names logs top-level in the same breath as venv ('~/.cairn/venv is correct - ONE venv per box, never one per device, and the same for logs and backups'). So 08-12 settled that logs IS a root; 08-18 settles its interior shape and gives the why. The two compose. THE RESIDUAL TENSION - device state living outside the device's space - dissolves on the ownership test itself: the <device>/<instance>/ segments beneath logs/ are an INDEX, not an ownership claim, and mirroring the code tree is addressing rather than owning.

THE RETENTION WHY MAKES THE NEW SHAPE PROTECT LAW 6 RATHER THAN STRAIN IT, and this is the argument that turns Akien's stated convenience ('easy to delete everything in the logs tree over 30 days old in one go') into a structural reason. address.py bounds itself explicitly: 'a shared helper that reached into every device's space to CREATE would be that failure written once and called convenient.' A 30-day sweep is that same reach in the DELETE direction, and delete is the more dangerous half. With trails scattered under 14 devices' own spaces the sweep must cross 14 gates; with one logs root it crosses none, because the logs root is nobody's device space. The convenience and the law want the same shape.

WHERE THE DEFAULT RECEIVER INSTALLS IS NOT SETTLED BY THIS CAST, and it is recorded as un-wrapped rather than smoothed over. Three shapes stand: (a) BaseDevice.__init__ wires a default receiver with a function-local import, keeping the module top import-light; (b) the writer LOWERS to cairn/tools/base/ as a floor-legal leaf and DiagnosticBase defaults to it, diagnostic_inspector keeping the reader half; (c) injection stays and every assembly point calls set_diagnostic_receiver. (c) IS ALREADY FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT - it is today's design, and it produced 3 production wiring sites against 15 emitting components. (b) is favoured on an in-house precedent of the identical shape, recorded in address.py itself: the roots table was 'Lowered here from cairn/machines/skill_block/counters.py on 2026-08-12 - the table was already injectable and already carried the why; what it lacked was an address the rest of the system could stand on.' BreadcrumbLog is in exactly that position. Favouring is not settling: the child a-device-logs-without-being-wired settles it against its own falsifier.

THE GRAIN IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A RULE, and nothing in this cast derives it. Akien drew the line by example - 'that doesn't mean every function call, or every heartbeat from the ground loop... but starting an inference call sure should. a probe firing at a gate crossing should' - so each emitter judges its own boundary crossings. This is left standing deliberately: a taxonomy of what-counts-as-major written now would be the reification failure this system keeps catching, and the falsifier's second arm (the inspector still needing a second exploration) is what would tell us the grain was wrong. If it goes wrong, the fix is evidence about real diagnoses, not a rule written in advance.

A NON-DEVICE CANNOT EMIT TODAY, and that is why the inference emitter is its own child. emit() arrives by inheriting BaseDevice; inference_domain is module functions and has zero emit sites, so Akien's flagship example - an inference call starting should log - is the one case the existing mechanism cannot reach at all. Giving it an emitter touches the standing open question open-what-grants-device-ness-once-definition-location-stops-being-evidence, which this intent did not mean to open and must not answer by accident.

CLAUSE (4) OF THIS TICKET'S FALSIFIER IS MEASURABLY RED AS OF 2026-08-18 13:20, and it gates this parent's crossing without needing a new ticket. It requires that the trails resolve under ONE root. They do not: the live ground loop (pid 973171, up 18h29m) is running code from before the address moved, and is still appending to ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/0/diagnostics.jsonl — the bus trail there took a record at 17:58 today. So two addresses are in use simultaneously, the old one holding the ONLY real history in instance-space (bus 312 records, ground_loop 168, spanning 2026-08-12 to 2026-08-18) and the new one holding nothing but proof exhaust until that process restarts. NOT ACTIONABLE BY CC: restarting Akien's Konsole-launched ground loop is out of bounds, and the migration of the six days already at the old address is his call — leave it, move it, or let it age out. Recorded here rather than cast as a fifth child because this ticket's own falsifier already covers it; a new ticket would be a second answer to a question this one already asks.

THIS DECOMPOSITION IS SHORT A CHILD, found 2026-08-18 while casting child (2) and recorded here rather than at this parent's crossing, where it would have been a dead voyage. The `falsifier` above carries FIVE clauses; `children` carries FOUR; and clause (3) — 'a probe firing at a gate crossing leaves one', which is Akien's own SECOND named example in the message that bore this ticket — is owned by none of the four. Child (1) closed the wiring for DEVICES and structurally could not reach it: measured at cairn/tools/base/shim.py:74, `class BaseShim(CoreValuesMixin, ABC)` carries no DiagnosticBase in its bases, so the component that fires probes has no emit() at all, and a shim is not a device.

IT IS THE SAME MISSING SHAPE AS CHILD (2), which is why it surfaced there and not here. inference_domain cannot emit because it has no class; BaseShim cannot emit because its class does not carry the mixin. Both reduce to one sentence — a component that is not a BaseDevice has no way to reach its own trail — and the floor seam child (2) builds (a trail scoped to a MODULE address rather than a class address, deriving its name through the same address.component_of_module the class side uses) is the same answer clause (3) needs. BaseShim's own fix is smaller still and may be one line in the bases.

NOT FOLDED INTO CHILD (2), deliberately: folding a sibling into a child is the shape Akien refused when he ruled child (4) a child rather than a fold ('folding it in would add a more specific into a less specific'), and the same objection runs the other way. It is a fifth child of THIS parent, uncast, and this parent cannot honestly cross PROVED against a falsifier one of whose clauses nobody owns.
